chunks.arabic_text: وَ رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْهُ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ:

translations.en: Muḥammad ibn Muslim narrated from him, peace be upon him, that he said:

chunks.arabic_text: «إِذَا صُمْتَ فَلْيَصُمْ سَمْعُكَ وَ بَصَرُكَ وَ شَعْرُكَ وَ جِلْدُكَ وَ عَدَّدَ أَشْيَاءَ غَيْرَ هَذَا»

translations.en: "When you fast, then let your hearing, your sight, your hair, and your skin fast as well," and he mentioned other things besides this.

chunks.arabic_text: وَ قَالَ «لَا يَكُونُ يَوْمُ صَوْمِكَ كَيَوْمِ فِطْرِكَ».

translations.en: And he said: "Let not the day of your fasting be like the day of your breaking the fast."

en.summary: This hadith teaches that sawm is not limited to refraining from food and drink, but includes restraining the senses and the body from improper acts. It emphasizes the ethical etiquette of fasting, so that a fasting day is spiritually distinct from an ordinary day.
en.seo_question: How should a believer's senses and conduct change while fasting?

key_terms.صُمْتَ: you fasted; entered the state of fasting
key_terms.فَلْيَصُمْ: then let it fast; a command to observe fasting in a broader moral sense
key_terms.سَمْعُكَ: your hearing; the faculty of listening that must be restrained
key_terms.بَصَرُكَ: your sight; the faculty of seeing that must be guarded
key_terms.جِلْدُكَ: your skin; the body, indicating bodily restraint during fasting
key_terms.صَوْمِكَ: your fasting; your day of sawm
key_terms.فِطْرِكَ: your breaking the fast; the state of not fasting
